record.paper_title: Spin-density-functional theory: some open problems and application to inhomogeneous Heisenberg models
record.original_question: What are the practical consequences for spin-density-functional-theory calculations of nonunique effective potentials in generalized density-functional theories, where the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem guarantees a one-to-one mapping between densities and wave functions but not necessarily between densities and potentials, and where systematic and accidental nonuniqueness can occur when more than one density variable is used?

evidence.quote: The question to what extent the effective potentials of SDFT (and other generalized DFTs) are uniquely determined by the densities arises because contrary to what is sometimes claimed in the literature, the standard proofs of the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem (by contradiction [22] and by constrained search [23]) guarantee only the existence of a one-on-one mapping between densities and wave functions, not densities and potentials.

Recently, examples have been given that show that nonuniqueness is not a pathological feature of single-electron systems, or limited to SDFT, but a general phenomenon, expected to occur whenever one works with more than one density variable [26, 27].
The implications of nonuniqueness for practical SDFT calculations are still under study [26, 28, 29, 31, 32].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a generalized density-functional theory in which the ground state of a many-electron system is described using more than one density variable (for example, in spin-density-functional theory the variables are the total electron density n(r) = n_↑(r) + n_↓(r) and the spin density m(r) = n_↑(r) − n_↓(r), with conjugate external potentials v(r) and a magnetic field B(r) coupling to the spin). The Hohenberg–Kohn theorem, proved either by contradiction or by constrained search, establishes a one-to-one mapping between the set of ground-state densities and the set of ground-state wave functions, but does not by itself establish a one-to-one mapping between the densities and the external potentials. It is known that "systematic" nonuniqueness (whole families of potentials yielding the same densities) and "accidental" nonuniqueness (isolated coincidences of densities from distinct potentials) can both occur whenever more than one density variable is used, and that this phenomenon is not restricted to single-electron systems or to spin-density-functional theory.

Problem. Determine, in a precise and quantitative way, the practical consequences of this nonuniqueness of the effective potentials for self-consistent Kohn–Sham–type calculations carried out within spin-density-functional theory (and other generalized density-functional theories employing multiple density variables). Specifically:

(a) Characterize the resulting failure of differentiability of the exchange-correlation energy functional E_xc[n, m] with respect to its density arguments, and identify the conditions under which only one-sided functional derivatives exist.

(b) Quantify the ambiguity in the Kohn–Sham effective potential v_s(r) and effective magnetic field B_s(r) that arises from this nonuniqueness, and describe how this ambiguity propagates to computed ground-state energies, spin densities, magnetic moments, and response properties such as susceptibilities and reactivity indices.

(c) Provide constructive prescriptions (e.g., a dual formulation minimizing with respect to potentials rather than densities, or a selection principle among admissible potentials) that yield well-defined and physically meaningful results, and assess to what extent existing approximate exchange-correlation functionals must be reinterpreted or modified to be consistent with such prescriptions.
artifact.status_search_result: The nonuniqueness of SDFT potentials is rigorously established (Capelle–Vignale 2001; lattice version Ullrich 2005). Subsequent work has clarified mathematical consequences: nondifferentiability of E_xc with respect to spin density, existence of one-sided derivatives, splitting of reactivity indices, and dual spin-potential functional formalisms. However, a complete and universally accepted prescription for handling these effects in practical self-consistent calculations, and a systematic reformulation of approximate functionals, remains under active development; the practical consequences are only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Nonuniqueness of the Potentials of Spin-Density-Functional Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit examples of distinct sets of potentials yielding the same ground-state densities; E_xc is not always a differentiable functional of the spin density.

status_evidence.title: Nonuniqueness in spin-density-functional theory on lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Demonstrates nonuniqueness as a generic phenomenon on lattices when more than one density variable is used.

status_evidence.title: Nonuniqueness of magnetic fields and energy derivatives in spin-polarized DFT
status_evidence.snippet: Nonuniqueness of B(r) implies nondifferentiability of energy functional w.r.t. spin density, but allows one-sided derivatives; reactivity indices split into one-sided descriptors.
status_evidence.claim: Partial resolution via one-sided derivatives and modified reactivity indices.

status_evidence.title: Spin-potential functional formalism for current-carrying noncollinear magnetic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Dual formalism minimizing with respect to spin potentials circumvents nonuniqueness issues.
status_evidence.claim: Dual formulation provides a constructive way to handle nonuniqueness.
